_comment: Gratitude Questionnaire-Six Item Form (GQ-6), McCullough, M. E., Emmons, R. A., & Tsang, J. (2002). The grateful disposition: A conceptual and empirical topography. Journal of Personality and Social Psychology, 82, 112-127. Items and scoring key taken verbatim from the author's own distributed scoring PDF (https://pages.ucsd.edu/~memccullough/gratitude/GQ-6-scoring-interp.pdf, fetched 2026-10-19), which states: 'The scale was published in a scientific journal for use in the public domain. You do not need to contact any of the authors for permission to use these scales in non-commercial research.' Registered per 12.gdx.virtology/GoDataX_H7ph_33_Virtudes_Instrumentos_Psicometricos.xlsx, which lists GQ-6 as the primary suggested instrument for the virtue 'Gratidao' (alongside VIA/IPIP-VIA Gratitude, not registered separately here to avoid a redundant second 'gratitude' construct). Catalog registration only -- no participant data collected or associated with this record.

study.title: Gratitude Questionnaire-Six Item Form (GQ-6) - Instrument Onboarding
study.objective: Register the GQ-6 (McCullough, Emmons & Tsang, 2002) as the source instrument for the Virtology virtue Gratidao, per GoDataX_H7ph_33_Virtudes_Instrumentos_Psicometricos.xlsx.
study.method: Official scale text and scoring key (McCullough, Emmons & Tsang, 2002); catalog registration only, no primary data collection associated with this record.

instruments.name: Gratitude Questionnaire-Six Item Form (GQ-6)
instruments.description: McCullough, M. E., Emmons, R. A., & Tsang, J. (2002). The grateful disposition: A conceptual and empirical topography. Journal of Personality and Social Psychology, 82, 112-127. Published in a scientific journal for public-domain, non-commercial research use.
instruments.instructions: Using the scale below as a guide, write a number beside each statement to indicate how much you agree with it: 1 = strongly disagree, 2 = disagree, 3 = slightly disagree, 4 = neutral, 5 = slightly agree, 6 = agree, 7 = strongly agree.
instruments.phenomenon_description: Individual differences in the tendency to notice and appreciate the positive in life, and to feel thankful for the contributions of others and of life circumstances to one's own well-being (McCullough, Emmons & Tsang, 2002).

constructs.name: Gratitude (GQ-6)
constructs.definition: Disposition to experience gratitude across a wide range of situations, people, and time -- the intensity, frequency, span, and density of gratitude as a trait (McCullough, Emmons & Tsang, 2002).

variables.name: Gratitude (GQ-6)
variables.description: Dispositional tendency to notice and appreciate the positive in life and feel thankful for it.
variables.operational_definition: Sum of 6 Likert items (4 positively keyed, 2 negatively keyed/reverse-scored), 1-7 scale each. Official scoring range 6-42.
variables.indicator_description: Sum of the 6 items, 2 reverse-scored before summing, per the official GQ-6 scoring key.

items.statement_text: I have so much in life to be thankful for.
If I had to list everything that I felt grateful for, it would be a very long list.
When I look at the world, I don't see much to be grateful for.
I am grateful to a wide variety of people.
As I get older I find myself more able to appreciate the people, events, and situations that have been part of my life history.
Long amounts of time can go by before I feel grateful to something or someone.
